title: Grounded Rao-Kupper Leaderboards for Music Arena

contributions.purpose: Model the 'both outputs are bad' (BOTH_BAD) arena outcome as a signal of absolute quality rather than discarding it.
contributions.mechanism: Grounded Rao-Kupper (GRK): extend the Rao-Kupper tie model by adding a constant 1 (a fictitious competitor with score 0) to the denominator, so P(BOTH_BAD)=1/(phi_i+phi_j+lambda*sqrt(phi_i*phi_j)+1) increases when both systems have low latent quality.
contributions.evaluation: Presented as a ranking model with a grounding anchor; validated via held-out NLL/Brier and ablations on Music Arena.
contributions.domain: Arena-style pairwise ranking / evaluation for generative AI (text-to-music)
contributions.source_quote: We propose Grounded Rao-Kupper (GRK), a ranking model that couples BOTH_BAD probability to model quality via a grounding anchor, treating BOTH_BAD as an outside option.

contributions.purpose: Show GRK improves over Bradley-Terry and a decoupled-badness baseline.
contributions.mechanism: Compare GRK against BT and AB-MNL (Additive Badness Multinomial Logit) on 4-way NLL and BOTH_BAD calibration, with bootstrap CIs and ablations removing the grounding mechanism.
contributions.evaluation: On Music Arena (3,274 battles, 12 systems, 983 test), GRK achieves 7.9% lower 4-way NLL (0.953 vs 1.035) and 12.4% lower BOTH_BAD Brier (0.187 vs 0.213), CIs exclude zero; per-class gain concentrated in BOTH_BAD (23% reduction).
contributions.domain: Ranking model evaluation for text-to-music arenas
contributions.source_quote: We demonstrate that GRK achieves statistically significant improvements over Bradley-Terry and decoupled baselines on Music Arena, with gains concentrated in BOTH_BAD prediction.

contributions.purpose: Validate that GRK's implied acceptability signal is meaningful and actionable.
contributions.mechanism: Compute GRK-implied P(BOTH_BAD | system vs average) and correlate with empirical BOTH_BAD rates across systems.
contributions.evaluation: Pearson r = 0.60 (p = 0.041) across 12 text-to-music systems, enabling quality-aware leaderboards reporting absolute acceptability.
contributions.source_quote: We show that GRK's implied acceptability signal correlates meaningfully with empirical BOTH_BAD rates (r = 0.60, p = 0.041), enabling quality-aware leaderboards that report absolute acceptability alongside relative rankings.

self_declared_provenance.quote: We propose Grounded Rao-Kupper (GRK), which treats BOTH_BAD as an outside option anchored to a fictitious competitor with score 0. By adding a constant 1 to the denominator of the Rao-Kupper model (Rao & Kupper, 1967), GRK creates a grounding anchor that couples BOTH_BAD probability directly to model quality.

Rao & Kupper (1967) extended this framework to accommodate ties by introducing a tie parameter ... However, none of these classical models can represent the BOTH_BAD outcome, which requires modeling absolute quality rather than just relative comparisons.
An alternative approach is to decouple 'badness' from skill by giving each system a separate badness parameter. We compare against AB-MNL (Additive Badness Multinomial Logit).
